Sirach 32:1: Have they appointed you leader? Do not exalt yourself. Be among them as one of them; take care of them, and then sit down.
Sirach 32:2: After attending to every duty, recline, so that you may rejoice because of them and receive a crown for good order.
Sirach 32:3: Speak, elder, for it is fitting for you, with exact knowledge, but do not hinder the music.
Sirach 32:4: Where there is a performance, do not pour out chatter or display wisdom at an unsuitable time.
Sirach 32:5: A carbuncle signet upon a golden ornament—so is an ensemble of musicians at a wine banquet.

Daniel 4:4: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, he said, “I was at peace in my house and prospering upon my throne.
Daniel 4:5: I saw a dream and became apprehensive; fear fell upon me.
Daniel 4:19: Daniel was greatly astonished, and apprehension pressed upon him. Frightened, seized with trembling, and changed in appearance, he shook his head and remained astonished for an hour. He answered me in a gentle voice, ‘O king, may this dream come upon those who hate you and its interpretation upon your enemies!
Daniel 4:20: You, O king, are the tree planted in the earth, whose appearance was great.
Daniel 4:21: And all the birds of heaven nesting in it—the strength of the earth and of the nations and of all languages to the ends of the earth, and all countries—serve you.
Daniel 4:22: The raising of that tree, its reaching heaven, and its mass touching the clouds mean that you, O king, were raised above all people upon the face of the whole earth. Your heart was raised in pride and strength against the Holy One and His angels. Your deeds were seen, because you laid waste the house of the living God on account of the sins of the consecrated people.
Daniel 4:23: The vision you saw, that an angel was sent in strength from the Lord and commanded the tree’s removal and cutting down, means that the judgment of the great God will come upon you,
Daniel 4:24: and the Most High and His angels are rushing against you.
Daniel 4:25: They will lead you away into custody and send you to a deserted place.
Daniel 4:26: The root of the tree that was left, since it was not uprooted, means that the place of your throne will be preserved for you for a time and an hour. Behold! They are preparing against you; they will scourge you and bring the judgments upon you.
Daniel 4:27: The Lord lives in heaven, and His authority is over all the earth. Entreat Him concerning your sins, and redeem all your injustices by almsgiving, so that gentleness may be granted you, you may have many days upon your royal throne, and He may not destroy you. Love these words, for my word is accurate and your time is full.’”
James 5:13: Is anyone among you suffering? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praise.
James 5:14: Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the elders of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the Lord’s name.
James 5:15: And the prayer of faith will save the weary sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
James 5:16: Therefore confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. A righteous person’s petition has great strength when it is at work.
James 5:17: Elijah was a human being with experiences like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain; and it did not rain upon the earth for three years and six months.
James 5:18: And he prayed again, and heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
